claims.text: A 5–10 µm tantalum interlayer between W and CuCrZr will enhance interfacial chemical bonding.
A 5–10 µm tantalum interlayer will alleviate thermo-mechanical stresses at the W/CuCrZr interface under fusion-reactor conditions.
W and CuCrZr joined without an interlayer have poor interfacial adhesion.
The poor adhesion of directly joined W and CuCrZr is caused by a mismatch in their coefficients of thermal expansion.
The proposed intervention uses sputtering to deposit a 5–10 µm Ta layer on W or CuCrZr.
The proposed deposited joint is diffusion annealed at 1200°C for 1 hour under vacuum.
Fusion-reactor operation involves high thermal loads, rapid thermal cycling, and neutron irradiation.
A thin Ta interlayer acts as a bridge between W and CuCrZr.
Ta has a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of tungsten and CuCrZr.
The intermediate thermal expansion of Ta bridges the thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
The Ta interlayer facilitates diffusion bonding during annealing.
Ta-assisted diffusion bonding relieves thermo-mechanical stresses and improves interfacial adhesion.
The Ta interlayer enhances resistance of the interface to degradation under neutron irradiation.
Relative to direct bonding, the Ta-containing interface will have improved interfacial bonding.
Relative to direct bonding, the Ta-containing interface will have reduced thermo-mechanical stresses.
Relative to direct bonding, the Ta-containing interface will have enhanced durability under fusion-reactor conditions.
A W/CuCrZr interface without an interlayer typically fails under high thermal and irradiation stresses.
